newsitem.title: USA: U.S. July existing home sales fell 0.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. July existing home sales fell 0.5 pct.

text.p: Sales of existing U.S. homes fell 0.5 percent in July to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 4.14 million units from a revised 4.16 million units in June, the National Association of Realtors said.
The July sales rate was up 4.3 percent from sales of 3.97 million in July last year.
Previously, NAR said June sales of existing homes fell 2.3 percent to 4.18 million units.
Wall Street economists had forecast July sales of 4.10 million units.

NAR Chief Economist John Tuccillo said "not too much should be read" into the July dip, because some slowdown was inevitable after a new record was set earlier this year in the pace of sales. Existing single-family home sales reached an all-time high in May when the rate was 4.28 million units.
He added that July's existing single-family home sales of 4.14 million, while a decline from June, were still higher than any month last year.
NAR President Art Godi said "interest rates are showing signs of leveling off."
The Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp's 30-year rate in July of 8.25 percent was a drop from June's 8.32 percent, which was the highest average so far this year.
